title: A Phase I/II Open-Label Extension of Study TIGEM1-MPSVI, Evaluating the Safety and Efficacy of FT005, an Adeno-Associated Viral Vector 8 to Deliver the Human ARSB Gene to the Liver of Subjects with Mucopolysaccharidosis type VI (MPS VI)
official: A Phase I/II Open-Label Extension of Study TIGEM1-MPSVI, Evaluating the Safety and Efficacy of FT005, an Adeno-Associated Viral Vector 8 to Deliver the Human ARSB Gene to the Liver of Subjects with Mucopolysaccharidosis type VI (MPS VI)
summary:
Primary safety objective: To evaluate the safety of systemic intravenous administration of AAV2/8.TBG.hARSB in pediatric MPS VI patients

Primary efficacy objective: To investigate the efficacy of the AAV2/8.TBG.hARSB through measurements of urinary GAGs, in pediatric MPS VI patients

interventions.name: Adeno-associated viral (AAV) serotype 8 (AAV2/8) vector with liver-specific thyroxin-binding globulin (TBG) promoter, driving the expression of the human ARSB gene

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Documented biochemical and molecular diagnosis of MPS VI
2. Subjects must be between 5 and 16 years of age (inclusive)
3. Subjects should have received ERT for at least 12 months before enrolment and should continue to receive ERT until 7-14 days before IMP administration
4. Documented informed consent; willingness to adhere to protocol and to participate to long-term follow-up, as evidenced by written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
1. Subjects unable or unwilling to meet requirements of the study
2. Systemic corticosteroid therapy or other immunosuppressive/immunomodulating drugs within 2 months prior to IMP administration
3. Female individuals of childbearing age who are pregnant or nursing or unwilling to use effective contraception for at least one year post-IMP administration
4. Fertile male individuals who are unwilling to use male barrier contraceptives such as condom
5. Any other condition that would not allow the subject to complete follow-up examinations during the study and that, in the opinion of the Investigator, would make the subject unsuitable for the study
6. Presence of serum NAB to AAV8 above the limit of detection of the assay (Screening)
7. Participation in any clinical study involving an investigational medicinal product within the 6 months preceding enrolment, or at any time during participation in this trial
8. Subjects unable to perform the 6MWT
9. History of severe anaphylactoid reaction to Naglazyme in subjects receiving ERT that could affect the safety (severe reaction is meant to be a respiratory impairment event that is life-threatening)
10. Presence of tracheostomy or need of ventilatory assistance
11. Subjects with evidence of progressive myelomalacia that is considered severe enough to require neck surgery in the first six months after enrolment
12. Values of AST or ALT above the upper limit of normal range
13. Co-existence of chronic diseases or clinically relevant abnormal laboratory values
14. Infections with hepatitis B, C, or HIV (screening)
